text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar rejected the criticism by a joint EU-Slovak parliamentary committe over democratic development in Slovakia, saying this committee had no competenece to decide on Slovakia's membership in European Union.
- Alexander Rezes, steel maker VSZ's supervisory board chairman, said Slovakia should start building a car producing plant by the end of 1999.

- Rezes said there were several foreign car producers interested in a possible car joint-venture in Slovakia, but added that Japanese car makers were still the strongest candidates for the cooperation.
- The European Democratic Union (EDU) has issued a statement saying that Slovakia has lost chances for early integration to western structures due to the leadership of the current government.
- Meciar said the ruling coalition was preparing its own law on direct presidential elections which should amend the entire constitution.

- Slovakia's Grafobal a.s., a major central Europe packaging materials producer, said it planned to increase its market share in the Czech Republic to around 30 percent in 1998, from the current 20 percent.
- Local dealers said the Slovak crown should move between the mark/dollar basket parity and around -0.80 percent on the band's weak side until the local money market returns to more stable trading.
SME - Premier Meciar said Slovakia would abolish its 20 percent import deposit measure within 14 days after the Czech Republic abolishes its similar deposit measure.
PRAVDA - Slovakia plans to expand by the year 2010 its river transport routes to the northern Slovak town of Zilina, some 160 kilometres north from the capital Bratislava.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovakia's sole oil refiner Slovnaft a.s. said it planned to spend some eight billion crowns on environmetal projects by the year 2010.
